gap: No retrieved work establishes whether passage-local context-triple supervision improves multi-hop KGQA at matched supervision volume, with an evaluation set the repair loop cannot edit, and with seed-level variance reported. The closest work size-matches the two disease KGs against each other (not the KG-grounded vs CG-grounded training arms), uses unequal numbers of repair examples across error categories, removes invalid triples from and regenerates validation questions in the set it reports 100% accuracy on, and evaluates only on synthetically generated items; separately, work on subgraph retrieval shows larger context adds noise. Consequently the causal claim (context content rather than more training signal) and the repair claim (repair rather than evaluation-set selection) are both unestablished.

evidence.quote: Since the original diabetes KG is much larger than the gastroparesis KG, we construct a size-matched diabetes subset to enable a fair comparison between the two disease settings.
Invalid triples are removed from the validation set, because repairing the model on unsupported or noisy facts would introduce incorrect supervision.
First, the QA datasets used for SFT, repair, RL, and evaluation are synthetically generated.
The desired subgraph is crucial as a small one may exclude the answer but a large one might introduce more noises.

why_unaddressed: The retrieved papers that construct context for the LLM do so either at inference (GraphRAG prompting) or without volume-matched controls; none of the analyzed works reports a token-matched or example-matched comparison between context-augmented and isolated-triple supervision, and none describes an evaluation split isolated from the repair loop. The closest work therefore leaves the decisive control unrun rather than solving it.
research_question: At matched supervision token budget and on a frozen, repair-blind held-out test split, does passage-local context-triple supervision (rather than added supervision volume) improve 3-5-hop KGQA accuracy over isolated-triple supervision?
potential_experiment: Four-arm factorial on one text-grounded corpus with a frozen test split: (A) isolated triples; (B) isolated triples padded with matched token volume of unrelated triples; (C) context triples from the same passage; (D) context triples plus repair. Match tokens and gradient steps across arms, report per-hop accuracy on the frozen test split with multiple seeds, and additionally run a context-size dose-response (0, k/4, k/2, k, 2k triples) to test for an inverted-U.
verification_required: Still to verify by reading the closest work's experimental section and appendix tables in full (only selected passages were read) that no matched-token or matched-example control and no untouched held-out split are reported; and to re-run the literature search once the paper budget allows, in case a recent paper already reports such controls.
